question: Should OpenClaw add a generic action-aware tool-policy contract for multiplexed tools, and what trusted approval or bypass semantics should approved workflows use?
rationale: Source inspection proves the missing generic action policy, but the fix defines a new authorization boundary and public config grammar that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Design Generic Action Policy
options.body: Add a typed action-aware policy grammar enforced before multiplexed actions execute, with documented precedence and trusted-context tests for message and gateway.

options.title: Narrow To Message And Gateway
options.body: Add separate action controls only for currently affected tools, reducing immediate scope while accepting parallel policy surfaces that may drift.

options.title: Defer To Confirmation Gate
options.body: Rely on the adjacent runtime confirmation work and accept that static least-privilege action deny remains unavailable for now.

recommendation.title: Design Generic Action Policy
recommendation.body: Add a typed action-aware policy grammar enforced before multiplexed actions execute, with documented precedence and trusted-context tests for message and gateway.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the partial message-action policy and prior review framing, and are the best available routing owner for the security/product decision.
